findings: The donor-to-body stream map is now substantially readable, but Devī is rendered as an ordinary fixed two-armed figure, contrary to the locked character rule that non-event-012 pages may foreground needed arms but must still imply her many-armed identity.
Devī is reduced to a fixed ordinary two-arm form, and the donor portraits use large disk halos despite the locked prohibition on unsourced halo symbolism.
The central figure does not preserve Devī's locked many-armed identity; the donor identities are otherwise differentiated and the prior lion is removed.
Only two arms are shown with no visual implication of the required many-armed identity.

Devī's prior weapon array and lion are removed, but event-010-style donor equipment and unrequested mounts remain visible, including Yama's rod, Indra's elephant and Sūrya's horse chariot, while the locked page-4 continuity records no equipment for these figures.
Several required donor portraits are cut by the left canvas edge, including portions of the Viṣṇu and Indra groupings, weakening complete donor readability.
The body-correspondence narration is much better supported, but the fixed two-arm Devī and later-stage donor equipment keep the image from satisfying the locked manifestation page as-is.
The exact x=0.08..0.92, y=0.06..0.24 rectangle is occupied across its lower portion by Shiva and Yama portraits, luminous disks, clouds and donor radiance.

findings.message: Retain the successful donor/body stream map while implying Devī's many-armed identity rather than depicting a fixed ordinary two-arm form.
Replace the large portrait disks with restrained source-bounded radiance that does not read as added halo iconography.
Keep this page on body formation only; remove donor weapons and unrequested mounts/chariots from the event-009 proof.
Move all portraits, clouds and radiance below y=0.24 within x=0.08..0.92.
